parsed.why: Most-protective tier: operating shield law, GI nondiscrimination, GI hate-crime cover, open M/F/X documents, custody by recognised gender identity. National passport/entry regime still binds every visitor, capping the score.

Long-standing nondiscrimination, GI hate-crime cover, shield law, open licence markers, conversion-therapy ban — but no in-force custody-by-identity protocol and a dated birth-sex placement case; national border regime still applies.

Hostile enacted laws (binary-sex codification, religious refusal statute, no state GI hate-crime cover) mostly enjoined by courts working for trans people; facilities bill restrained. Above parent average, well below protective states.

Most-protective tier: shield law, statewide GI nondiscrimination since 2006, GI hate-crime penalties, self-attested X markers, gender-neutral single-occupancy restrooms, city self-determination bathroom ordinance. National entry/document regime remains the ceiling.

National legislature's facilities ban in force locally, unrepeatable locally; trans protesters arrested Dec 2024; national document, entry and custody regimes apply directly with no documented local mitigation beyond a fragile low-risk ranking.
